subject: Clarify order form packaging tiers, price anchoring, and floor protections
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@datasymmetry.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@datasymmetry.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on pricing exhibits / caps & floors in order form

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the draft order form you shared last week. Our legal and finance teams reviewed Exhibit P and had a couple of items that need clarification before we can route for signature:

1) Cap vs floor language — the current wording references a "price floor" and a separate "stabilization cap" but it's not clear how the two interact during ramp months. If usage drops into the floor band, do we owe the minimum fee or is there a true-up only once quarterly?

2) Packaging / tier anchoring — the three-tier packaging (Starter / Growth / Enterprise) includes stair-step discounts at volume thresholds. We need an explicit example calculation in the exhibit so our procurement can map to our budget.

3) Concessions & transitional credits — because we are moving several workloads in Q3, we'd like to request a short-term discount (10% for 60 days) or a credit to offset migration costs.

Can you loop in legal and finance to confirm intended mechanics? We prefer an explicit reconciliation cadence (30-day rolling average or calendar quarter) and a sample calc row.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Amelia Torres
VP, Cloud Platform
DataSymmetry, Inc.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@datasymmetry.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing exhibits / caps & floors in order form

Amelia —

Appreciate the clear list. Per your request I've looped in Karthik (commercial) and Laura (legal) to confirm the intended reconciliation flow and packaging examples. Quick answers up front:

- Intent: floors are minimum monthly fees that trigger if monthly billable usage falls below the committed threshold. The stabilization cap is a temporary mechanism to limit upside (protect you from spike-driven bill increases) only during the initial 90-day migration window. They do not both apply to the same month; Exhibit P contains the priority order but we can make that explicit.

- Reconciliation cadence: we usually do a calendar-quarter true-up, but for customers moving production in the first month we can agree to a 30-day rolling average for the first 90 days.

- Transitional credit: we can offer a one-time migration credit or a 10% discount for the first 60 days. I'll confirm the commercial approval.

Attaching the latest working draft for reference: Draft_Orderform_v3.pdf (see Exhibit P, pricing table examples).

Next steps: Laura will propose redline language, Karthik will confirm the short-term concession, and Rachel will outline how the finance team prefers to capture the credit on the invoice. Can we aim to finalize wording by end of week?

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Draft_Orderform_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 230 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing exhibits / caps & floors in order form

Jordan / team —

Thanks — a few commercial notes to make the redline practical for procurement:

• Packaging anchor: replace the abstract "tier discount schedule" with a worked example row in Exhibit P showing: monthly usage (tokens), per-token unit price, applied discount, resulting line item. That keeps procurement from guessing.

• Floor mechanics: recommend the floor be expressed as a monthly minimum fee equal to X% of committed ARR (or explicit $ amount) with quarterly true-up. For customers migrating, allow a 30-day rolling true-up for first 90 days.

• Cap interaction: propose language that the stabilization cap applies only to bills generated within the first 90 days of go-live and is calculated before any migration credit is applied. That ensures caps don't obscure credit economics.

• Short-term concession: commercial can approve a 10% promotional discount applied to subscription fees for the first two billing cycles (60 days) conditioned on >50% workload migration. If they don't hit the migration milestone, the discount will be reclaimed as a credit offset in the next invoice.

I'll leave the exact wording to legal, but this is the commercial guardrail we want. Rachel — please confirm if finance can accept reclaiming the discount as an invoice-level credit.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Commercial Strategy

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing exhibits / caps & floors in order form

Team —

Attached is a proposed redline for Exhibit P that addresses Amelia's questions and incorporates Karthik's commercial points. Key elements:

1) Priority and interaction: Added a short paragraph that sets priority: (i) migration credits and promotional discounts are applied after calculation of capped bill amounts but before application of any floor true-up amounts. This avoids double-counting.

2) Floor definition: Replaced vague references with explicit formula: "Monthly Minimum Fee" = Max(Declared Monthly Commit in Section 1, $X) where $X is the agreed dollar floor. True-ups occur on a calendar-quarter basis; for the initial 90-day migration period true-ups will use a 30-day rolling average.

3) Stabilization cap: Clarified that the stabilization cap limits customer exposure to monthly bill increases above the Baseline Rate for a 90-day window; cap calculation is performed on pre-credit, pre-discount amounts.

4) Worked example: Inserted a sample calculation table showing a hypothetical 30-day usage, unit price, discount applied, migration credit, and resulting invoice line.

5) Reclaim mechanics: Added language that any promotional discount is conditionally applied and may be reclaimed as an invoice-level credit if migration milestones are not met, with 30 days notice to customer.

I included tracked changes in OrderForm_Exhibit-P_redline.docx. Please review and confirm commercial acceptability before I send to Amelia. If approved, I will prepare a clean copy for signature and a DocuSign envelope link.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
Attachments: OrderForm_Exhibit-P_redline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 45 KB)

Amelia —

Thanks for raising these — and apologies for the earlier ambiguity. Laura attached a redline that clarifies the interaction of floor, cap, discounts and migration credits, plus a worked example for procurement. Commercial has approved a conditional 10% migration discount for the first 60 days (see redline for milestones).

Next steps:
